description: Reads back and forth inside the soundfile at random zigzag timepoints, playing the source backwards whenever it moves from a later to an earlier time. Pinned to submode 1 (random zigzags between 'start' and 'end', beginning at file start and ending at file end); submode 2 (user-supplied timefile) can be curated separately. Stochastic: unseeded runs differ; the -r seed gives exact reproducibility (verified byte-identical decoded samples for seed 1 run twice). IMPORTANT: 'dur' is a floor, not a target — see known_issues.
musical_use: Extends material by slipping and sliding through it, with genuine backwards playback on every reverse leg — which transmutes the source much more than scramble-style concatenation. Long zigs create a powerful warping, tape-hand-winding effect; short zigs (small minzig/maxzig) give stuttering, repeated-note figures. A good first step for pushing recognisable material toward the abstract while keeping its continuity, since legs are spliced smoothly rather than cut.

start.description: Together with 'end', defines the time interval of the infile within which the zigzag timepoints fall.

end.description: End of the zigzag interval in the infile (must be greater than 'start' and no more than the infile duration).

dur.description: Total output duration requested. Empirically a minimum: CDP keeps zigzagging until it can finish at the file end, overshooting by a stochastic amount (observed +5% to +53% for dur=5 on a 2 s input). Treat the duration-model prediction as a lower bound.

minzig.description: Minimum acceptable time between successive zigzag timepoints. Small values (e.g. 0.05-0.2) give stuttering textures; larger values give sweeping warps.

splicelen.description: Length of the splice slope in milliseconds (CDP default 25 ms; the engine emits it explicitly). Scalar only.

maxzig.description: Maximum acceptable time between successive zigzag timepoints. Scalar only.

seed.description: Seed (> 0) for a replicable random sequence — the same seed reproduces the output exactly (verified). Omitted (CDP default 0): a different random sequence every run, seeded from the clock.

examples.description: Extend a 2 s source to roughly 6 s of sliding, warping motion over its full span.
examples.expected_use: Warped, back-and-forth extension of the whole file; seeded so the result is reproducible.

examples.description: Stuttering repeated-note figure from a narrow region.
examples.expected_use: Rapid short zigzags inside half a second of material — a stutter/tremolo gesture.

known_issues: 'dur' is a floor, not a target: mode 1 must end at the file end, so CDP keeps zigzagging past 'dur' until a final leg can land there. Observed outputs for dur=5 on a 2 s input: 5.25-7.64 s across seeds (up to +53%, and more than dur + indur is possible). The set_by duration model is deliberately retained as the best available lower-bound predictor — 'static' (= indur) would be far worse for an extend process — but no duration row is pinned in the shared formula table because the prediction is not within 5%.

Stochastic, and unseeded runs take their seed from the clock: two runs launched within the same second return byte-identical audio; runs a second apart differ. Pass 'seed' for reproducibility. Stereo seed-linking machinery (linking separate mono runs by seed) lands later; channels within a single multi-channel file already share one zigzag path.
Some (params, seed) combinations abort with 'ERROR: Final zig too short for splicelen.' (observed with seed 7 on a 2 s input) — retry with a different seed or a shorter splicelen.
All six numeric parameters reject breakpoint files ('ERROR: Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').
